#59974. Manchester United’s fitness levels are like that of a Sunday league team - no wonder they appointed Mauricio Pochettino

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1108 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fourfourtwo ↗ Open Full Page

Manchester United’s fitness levels are like that of a Sunday league team - no wonder they appointed Mauricio Pochettino

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that manchester United made the first managerial change of the season.
  • Sources indicate that in fairness, Carrick’s dismissal shouldn’t have come as a surprise.
  • And, as has been the custom for recent years, United decided to chop and change for the fifth successive time in the period between October and January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that manchester United made the first managerial change of the season. Not even spirited back-to-back comebacks against AS Roma and Aston Villa could save Michael Carrick.

Sources indicate that in fairness, Carrick’s dismissal shouldn’t have come as a surprise. After 10 games, Man United sit 18th. They’re sole league win was at home against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

And, as has been the custom for recent years, United decided to chop and change for the fifth successive time in the period between October and January. Their last five permanent managers have bitten the dust in this window, dating back to Jose Mourinho.

To say that United are a club littered with issues would be an understatement. They splashed the cash to rebuild their midfield over the summer, an area that was in need of dire investment.

Recent findings suggest that elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes were top targets to sort their complications in the middle of the park. They missed out on the pair, who moved to Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur, respectively.

Instead, they ended up with Andrey Santos, who struggled to force his way into the Chelsea starting XI; Youri Tielemans, a player that in fairness boasts ample Premier League experience and a history of avoiding major injuries; and Carlos Baleba.

The latter joined 12 months too late, but arrived at a fraction of the price Brighton & Hove Albion demanded the previous summer. Even then, the Cameroonian has played just 397 minutes of competitive action due to fitness issues.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a recent development, they neglected other areas, however. The centre-backs aren’t up to scratch. Joshua Zirkzee isn’t up to the task of deputising for Benjamin Sesko. The full-backs don’t have the footballing brain to help restore United to their former glory. All of this would be masked if the team was at least trying to hurt opponents.

This is the major concern for United. Yes, the players may not be the most technically gifted. But if they are at least outrunning their opponents, outfighting the team they’re up against, then it gives them a greater chance of securing a result. This is where United fall down, and worryingly so.

Recent findings suggest that it was in August that newly introduced arrival Tielemans said to former United centre-back Rio Ferdinand: “When you come back from the World Cup, you don't do loads of running. Just chill.” Ferdinand was shocked as the Belgian admitted that the players used pre-season to focus on ball-work rather than fitness. This has had some positive effects on the squad. United rank top for chances created per 90 (14.5) in the Premier League this season.

317 touches in the opposition box ranks fifth. An 85.5% pass success rate is also up there as one of the best. Rather, the matter comes when United don’t have the ball. This is where they fall down, and they fall hard.

Using Gradient Sports, a football analysis organization, we can see just how poor they’ve been out of possession, namely in the key metrics that can prove the difference between victory and defeat when the going gets tough. After all, this United side has covered just 1,066.8km in England’s top tier this season, the second-lowest (19th) in the league.

Recent findings suggest that an average max speed of 30.2km/h is also 19th. A sprinting distance of 23.7km is 13th. High-speed running distance of 65.0km is worse still, at 17th. 375.8km walking is the third-highest. Even if they were jogging into position to regain some semblance of shape, it would be easier on the eye. They’re not even doing that. A jogging distance of 456.1km ranks 19th.

In short, it’s a United side that isn’t busting a gut to minimise pressure on their own goal. Nor is it one that can last the full 90 minutes. They’ve either started matches slowly or faded in the latter stages of matches this season. When you’re a team playing a game every three days, that simply isn’t good enough. The opening weekend defeat at Hull City should have served as a real wake up call.

Now, they’ll be hoping the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino will provide just that. The Argentine is renowned for his brutal fitness demands. You can bet that these United players will have received a much-needed kick up the backside. It’ll be the most intense couch to 5k of their lives. "First of all he made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal,” former Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur centre-back Toby Alderweireld told the BBC earlier this month.

Industry observers note that “The way he wants to play - on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play - you need to run. You need to be capable of running and be capable of high intensity runs - the basic is to be fit.

“Every manager wants a good pre-season and time to give the players their ideas and the fitness. But the players are going to feel straight away that it's a different level.”.

According to recent reports, it’s a shame for United that Pochettino has minimal time to work with the squad ahead of the trip to Liverpool. A meeting with the Reds at Anfield is never easy to navigate. For a team managed by the demanding Andoni Iraola, it would be a miracle if this United squad isn’t running on fumes for the final knockings of Sunday’s clash. They’re already starting on the backfoot.

In time, though, Pochettino will whip this United side into shape. The results may not be clear at first now that we’re past the final international break of the year. With the games coming thick and fast, there won’t be much time on the training pitch. Upping the ante fitness wise is the first hurdle the squad needs to overcome. Steer the club on the straight and narrow, and it won’t be long before United begin to pull away from danger.

#59970. Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2243 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2243 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • UPCOMING YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPCOMING YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game initiative that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during New York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

It has been revealed that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

Sources indicate that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness issues over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill noted. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In a recent development, in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

It has been revealed that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two vital blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of New York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

In the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas stated. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match initiative that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

According to recent reports, the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a plan," Armas remarked. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

In a recent development, gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while presently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros stated. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

Industry observers note that more importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up initiative for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull New York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce noted. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

Sources indicate that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

"I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros remarked. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

According to recent reports, "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With a stylish assist and a gorgeous goal, Viktor Gyokeres produced the sort of match-winning performance that suggests the Swedish striker is making significant progress at last. It has not always been straightforward for him at Arsenal, but this was unquestionably one of his better showings, and it continued an encouraging upturn in his form.

It has been revealed that gyokeres has been the second-choice striker for most of this season, with Mikel Arteta usually preferring the more subtle Kai Havertz in attack. There are signs, though, that Gyokeres is now growing in belief. Following this victory over Slavia Prague, which was much more narrow and nervy than it should have been, he has now scored two goals and registered three assists in his last five appearances.

Industry observers note that even more promising than those statistics was his all-round play in Prague. In the first half especially, Gyokeres held on to long passes, combined with his team-mates and tested the opposition with his runs in behind. For Arsenal’s first goal, he found Noni Madueke with a brilliant pass. For their second, he curled a fabulous strike into the top corner.

It has been revealed that “Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”.

Industry observers note that those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

“We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” noted Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”.

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

It has been revealed that the goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

Just as Gyokeres is finding his form, so is Madueke. The absence of the injured Bukayo Saka has given Madueke a run in the side and he seems to be benefiting from it, even if he still lacks the same consistency in decision-making as his England team-mate.

One of Slavia’s many problems in a one-sided first half was their inability to cope with Arsenal’s rotations in midfield. Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Merino were all alternating positions at will, taking turns to drop deep and push forward. Merino could have scored a couple, before he combined sharply with Gyokeres for Arsenal’s second.

Gyokeres has never been the most delicate link-up player, and there have been too many times when the ball has simply bounced off him, but here he was impressively sleek. A quick exchange of passes with Merino allowed him a sight of goal, and the curled finish was sumptuous. For a man known for his power, this was an uncharacteristic demonstration of finesse.

Industry observers note that game over? Arsenal clearly thought so. They certainly came out for the second half like a team that believed the job was done. Arteta became increasingly irate in the first few minutes after the restart, with Ben White on the receiving end of one verbal slap. Rice also received a telling-off, and a yellow card, from the referee after kicking the ball away in annoyance.

Would Slavia have secured a draw if they had been at full strength? They had been weakened by the banishment of their star striker from the club because of a series of disciplinary failings. Tomás Chory, the top scorer for the past two seasons, was chucked out of the team after showing his middle finger to the referee in a recent game. This sort of sanction would have earned Arteta’s approval, no doubt, but it did not increase Slavia’s chances of hurting the Premier League champions in those edgy final few minutes.

Perhaps they will reflect on that decision differently now, given the uncharacteristically wobbly second-half performance by Arsenal. The visitors were vulnerable in the latter stages, when they lacked the control and composure that Arteta expects. Gabriel, too, appeared dismayed by what he was seeing. At one point, he put his hands on his hips and scowled at his team-mates like an angry teacher.

Recent findings suggest that with only a few minutes remaining, Nowak converted a left-wing cross to plunge Arsenal into a proper panic. It required a backs-to-the-wall defensive action, similar to the victory against Liverpool on Sunday, to get over the line.

Always we need to value winning away in the Champions League. It is extremely difficult. Two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn’t do it. Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.

We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn’t do that we had to go and do that in the second half.

We made six changes but we know the quality of the players we have. Whether we were lacking something I don’t know but I would have done the same thing [again].

I value what the team has done now, it is 11 away games we played, but our standards should be higher.

Arteta on Gyokeres: "He was really good. A game we believed was good for him, for the spaces he could use. He was really connected to the team. Great news because I think he needed that. Really pleased.".

According to recent reports, arteta: "Two very different halves. The first we played at a really high level. At half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning we were extremely far from our standards. Very far from the standards we expect from each other.".

Industry observers note that first half we played really, really well. We created a lot of chances and could have scored more but the second half was completely different. They stepped up a gear and made it difficult for us and we have to learn from it. Delighted with the win but a lot of things to improve going forward.

Industry observers note that maybe they started pressing a bit higher with more intensity. We had too many giveaways especially in the final third. There was too much running from box to box and we have to manage those reactions and go for the third and fourth goal.

At the end of the day it is three points.

Slavia Prague managed just one shot on goal in the first half worth 0.12 xG but finished the game with 18 shots on Arsenal’s goal and 2.23 xG. Arsenal could easily have dropped points on the balance of the second 45 minutes.

Slavia Prague XI: Domchak, Holes, Zima, Vlcek, Suleiman, Moses, Sadilek, Kubiak, Ayaosi, Sturm, Nowak.

Good evening from a chilly Prague, where Arsenal are looking for a repeat of the 3-0 victory they secured here exactly one year ago. It’s a remarkable coincidence that Mikel Arteta’s team have travelled to face Slavia Prague on November 4th in back-to-back years.

It has been revealed that on that occasion last year, Max Dowman became the youngest player in Champions League history. He should get more minutes tonight from the bench, given that he is presently suspended from Premier League action following his controversial red card against Fleetwood last week.

That’s the most Arteta has rotated between a Premier League and Champions League game so far this season. Telling perhaps that Konsa, Gabriel and Rice – the team’s defensive bedrock – stay in place. But changes on both sides at full-back, and in the attacking midfield areas.

Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Zubimendi, Merino; Madueke, Gyokeres, Eze.

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Saliba, Mosquera, Timber, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard, Guimaraes, Tzolis, Dowman, Havertz.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Six changes for our Champions League test 👊.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s critics will still grumble about the style of victory, but, of all clubs, this is a team who have no obligation to play in a way that neutrals might enjoy. Arsenal spent so much of Arsene Wenger’s 22-year reign playing football that was mostly stylish but only sometimes effective in big games. Now they are mostly effective but only occasionally stylish on such occasions. If you asked all the travelling fans at Anfield which they prefer, you would receive an overwhelming response.

According to recent reports, david Raya has kept a clean sheet in 54% of his Champions League starts (21 clean sheets from 39 starts), the best ratio of any goalkeeper to start at least 25 games in the competition. 🤯🇪🇸 https://t.co/A1Zpn8kJN9.

Arsenal return to Slavia Prague for the third time under Mikel Arteta knowing that three points will be another step towards a top-eight finish in the Champions League league phase.

Arteta’s team were 4-0 winners in the Czech capital in a 2021 Europa League quarter-final second leg, and 3-0 victors at this stage of the Champions League a year ago. Bukayo Saka opened the scoring with a penalty before two second-half goals from Mikel Merino.

Paris-St Germain are top of the table on 12 points after their rout against Villarreal last night. Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis are the three teams who have the chance to join them on maximum points. Arsenal will jump to 10 points with a win, above Bayern Munich, Sporting and Aston Villa at a minimum.

Slavia Prague are top of the Czech league and unbeaten after 13 games this season, but they are winless in the Champions League after fixtures against Lens, Sabah and Fernerbahce.

The fixture should be a presentable opportunity for Arteta to rotate his team, especially after a physically taxing game at Anfield where Arsenal revealed their mettle to win at Liverpool’s home for the first time since 2012.

Arsenal’s second-string is very strong, though they did not cover themselves in glory at Fleetwood in the League Cup last week when Max Dowman was sent off. Given the 16-year-old is banned for another two Premier League games, and the attention Arteta’s touchline reaction to the red card attracted, one wonders if he might want to seize a chance to put Dowman back on the horse.

Industry observers note that william Saliba’s return to full training is very welcome news, despite Ezri Konsa impressing in his absence. Saliba travelled with the squad to Prague, and could make his first appearance of the season following a back injury which flared up in France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain. With fixtures against Manchester City, Borussia Dortmund, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid, Bournemouth and Manchester United before the end of 2026 though, they will not want rush him.

Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze are other players pushing for greater involvement from the start of matches.

Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.
  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

Recent findings suggest that none of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

In a recent development, tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

In a recent development, with Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

In a recent development, their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

Sources indicate that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of fresh players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely key but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Tech Report: Mauricio Pochettino's final go with USMNT is all about pivoting to the future before Manchester United move

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S.
  • It has been revealed that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • According to recent reports, "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

It has been revealed that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

According to recent reports, "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that claims it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his looks for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino stated. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

According to recent reports, for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an important latest chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

Sources indicate that as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his latest role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

In a recent development, two years removed from starting a latest job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

According to recent reports, "For me, it's not difficult," he mentioned of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders have so far found compromises in response to many of US President Donald Trump's demands.

But they were surprised to hear Trump say that he raised Europe's security framework with Russian officials.

"It's going to be a significant agreement and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump said after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House last week.

In a recent development, he said that deal might include all of Europe. But what he meant by "all of Europe" was not clear.

US envoy Jared Kushner also wrote that Europe and Russia had struggled to establish a sustainable security framework for more than 30 years and that he was looking at "broader" European security architecture before he was to fly to Abu Dhabi.

That sent off alarm bells in European capitals, with diplomats having pushed back on Washington's approach to secure a peace deal in Ukraine.

They feared that a peace settlement could restore Russia's sphere of influence and undermine NATO.

Sources indicate that "We ​already have European security ​architecture in place. NATO and the European Union both have their ​respective roles. We ​must make sure Ukraine is integrated ‌into ⁠this architecture," remarked Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief.

Russia made clear during talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week that they were keen to discuss a broader European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"Phrases about the European security architecture are certainly Russian talking points and not only talking points but, to a degree, part of a media propaganda effort that Russia makes to frame the war as it wishes to frame the war," remarked Michael Kimmage, a historian of the Cold War.

Russian leaders, including Vladimir Putin, have long alleged that the US and NATO repeatedly violated pledges they made in the early 1990s not to expand the alliance into the former Soviet bloc.

They have seen NATO's enlargement during this period as having put them in a humiliating position in which they could do very little.

At the same time, in the 1990s, the European project saw the birth of the European Union, the single market that ensured the free movement of goods and people across member states, the Schengen agreement for border-free travel, and the euro.

The core idea was to extend peace across the continent.

"Europe can mean so many things, but the European project was not designed for war. It was designed for peace," remarked Kimmage.

During this period, there were even suggestions of Russia becoming a NATO member.

But that relative period of stability changed after Russia invaded Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and debuted its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Industry observers note that "Russia wants to redraw all of this by force. And I think that that's fundamentally unacceptable to Europe with all the diversity and variations that you get within the European landscape on what's acceptable and not acceptable. I think the large-scale redrawing of borders by force is just not the European project," stated Kimmage.

"So to the extent that the redrawing of borders by force is the lifeblood of Russian foreign policy, and I think that's a pretty easy case to make, Russia and Europe are at an impasse," he remarked.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Trump administration very quickly turned to making sure that "existing European security institutions" would be intact, with Jared Kushner having remarked late Thursday that the next round of negotiations would include "our European partners.".

Kushner, along with Steve Witkoff, flew to Moscow to talk to Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi. Then they flew to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Kushner had earlier Thursday signaled some "really incredible" postwar plans for Ukraine, saying that it could not be concluded without Europeans at the table.

"We should not allow a diktat from Russia that would result in some kind of neutralization or significant reduction in the military forces of Ukraine going forward, because that would make Ukraine very, very vulnerable to future aggression and pressure coming from Russia," mentioned Hiski Haukkala, the director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.

That would mean that Ukraine would also be completely dependent on the security guarantees that the US or Europeans are able and willing to provide.

Recent findings suggest that "We are supporting Ukraine because we are supporting international law and the basic norms of decency and international security when it comes to European security architecture. And this is the vantage point from which we are operating," he said.

The European Union has repeatedly pointed to some of the basic treaties that Russia broke, including:.

Recent findings suggest that "Russia walked away from these principles and smashed them to pieces in the process. And they are not interested in reinstating the previous security architecture order. They want something different in its stead. And as long as this is not on the table, the Russian form of negotiation is to wage war. War is a form of bargaining," Haukkala said.

"And they are signaling strategic intent to change the makeup of European security, to subdue Ukraine and to change the very essence of European security," he added.

Sources indicate that daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for European Affairs in the George W. Bush administration, noted Russia is very good at sticking to its demands.

He said Russians know how to negotiate and "right now, they are not negotiating," referring to talks in Abu Dhabi.

Some experts noted there was no possibility of having a new security architecture with the Russians at this point because there was no trust or common vision to align with Russia at the moment.

"There is no obvious compromise — dismantling NATO and the EU is not an option for Europe," mentioned Maria Snegovaya, an expert on Russia at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank.

"Repeatedly offering Putin peace deals he is unwilling to accept will not produce that outcome," Snegovaya noted.

Others like Balazs Jarabik, an expert on post-Soviet politics, said that Russia was part of the European security architecture whether Europeans liked it or not.

"And the question is whether it's included as our enemy. Obviously, Russia is not going to be a partner, right? We have to find a modus operandi to reduce the risk of a horizontal escalation and potentially a bigger European war, even a bigger one than what we have now.".

A host of European leaders on Friday rejected the Russian demands to discuss Europe's security framework as well, with a spokesperson for the German government saying that Berlin was looking to host a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" to secure funding for Ukraine's defense and reach a unified position regarding future peace talks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since replacing Sepp Blatter amid a corruption scandal in 2016, FIFA president Gianni Infantino has solidified his grip on world football’s governing body.

He expanded the men's World Cup to 48 teams, introduced VAR, and has significantly increased development funding for member federations - a move that ensured his unchallenged re-election in 2019 and 2023.

However, the political landscape has shifted this past year, following a fierce backlash against his aborted plan to sell stakes in World Cup profits to private investors. In short, Infantino’s uncontested reign is officially over.

Sources indicate that two football administrators have formally submitted their candidatures, securing the necessary backing from five member federations. When the 211 member associations vote in Morocco on March 18, 2027, Infantino will face two very different challengers.

Here is a look at the two men attempting to unseat him.

Sources indicate that philippe Diallo represents the most direct threat to Infantino. The 63-year-old took over as president of the French Football Federation (FFF) in 2023, and although a relatively recent arrival into the upper echelons of international football politics, he is a veteran sports administrator.

Backed by UEFA, who have spearheaded the resistance against Infantino, Diallo’s campaign is built upon reform and transparency.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that diallo has served on the UEFA Executive Committee and balanced domestic reform in France while overseeing a period of success for the national team and women’s game. He recently implemented a major grassroots initiative in France aimed at doubling registered female players to 500,000.

Diallo has lodged a direct attack on Infantino’s 'solitary governance', publicly questioning FIFA’s strategy of seeking private billions when the governing body already holds vast cash reserves.

Sources indicate that “My vision is that of open governance,” Diallo recently stated. “It's one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general.”.

Sources indicate that from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Kohzo Tashima brings a different background to the election. Tashima, 69, is a former Japanese international who transitioned into coaching youth national teams before climbing the administrative ladder.

Sources indicate that tashima’s experience is embedded in the traditional structures of the sport and served as the president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024. He right now holds the title of honorary president. He has also served on both the FIFA Council and the AFC executive committee, earning a reputation as a reliable bureaucrat.

While Diallo focuses on the opacity of Infantino’s reign, Tashima's campaign hinges on a platform of restoring moral authority to FIFA.

Industry observers note that after his candidacy was officially submitted by the JFA, Tashima emphasised the need for a stronger sense of ethics at the top of world football. “We will share with the world the importance of fair play, respect and integrity,” he mentioned. He has vowed to make FIFA a "healthier and more trusted organisation.".

The 2027 election in Morocco could be the most closely contested battle for the definitive seat of world football in generations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be key for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

"I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen said following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

Industry observers note that his growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also showed when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

"I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

You can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system reveals in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

Industry observers note that "He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that big of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach said. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really notable as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

Recent findings suggest that while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

According to recent reports, of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • It has been revealed that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

It has been revealed that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has debuted its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

Industry observers note that the IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company confirmed that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a new governance structure that it states is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of newly introduced medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei noted in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

According to recent reports, the firm has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, revealed partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and said it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We strategy to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

It has been revealed that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the firm hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

According to recent reports, some of the company’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a latest CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

In a recent development, in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

“Expectations are sky high,” says Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

But Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the company was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

On 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at Newly introduced York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic declared the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

In another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

Anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

City, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

Industry observers note that for all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

According to recent reports, the Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a latest proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

Sources indicate that these two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.
  • McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.

McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

The result continues the teenager’s brilliant week after she broke the 400m freestyle world record last Tuesday – breaking defending Olympic champion Ariarne Titmus’ previous record of 3:56.40, which was set last May, in a time of 3:56.08.

Speaking after her latest triumph, McIntosh shared her emotions.

“That’s the first time I really vividly heard the crowd during my race,” McIntosh mentioned, per Reuters.

According to recent reports, “It’s amazing to have all my family and friends in the stands, cheering me on. It really helped me in the last 100 meters.”.

The Canadian teen made her Olympic debut aged 14 at Tokyo 2020, where she finished fourth in the 200-meter freestyle.

She bagged gold in the 200m butterfly and 400m medley at the world championships in 2022, as well as two golds at the Commonwealth Games in the 200m and 400m medleys.

She now trains in Florida under coach Brent Arckey with the Sarasota Sharks team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

Recent findings suggest that OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

In a recent development, fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:.

According to recent reports, wednesday, Nov. 18BK Hacken vs. Manchester City, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)Real Madrid vs. Inter, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-Germain, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Juventus vs. OH Leuven, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Thursday, Nov. 19 Austria Wien vs. Bayern Munich, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Paris FC vs. HB Koge, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)  Arsenal vs. OL Lyonnes, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Barcelona vs. Servette, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Benfica vs. Roma, 3 p.m. (Paramount+).

It has been revealed that fans could get a glimpse of a future round when Arsenal take on OL Lyonnes on Thursday. The Gunners now have the tall task of tackling the French giants after battling Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at Camp Nou last week.

Sources indicate that A strong team defensive performance, anchored by goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez against the current title holders, and the inclusion of Frida Maanum in the attack were key difference-makers. Manager Renee Slegers and her side seem to be turning the page, with better results after questionable tactics and player availability raised concerns about the club's earlier performances.

Taking on OL Lyonnes also won't be easy. The top French side has scored 20 goals through four league phase matches, and Marie-Antoinette Katoto leads the competition's Golden Boot race with seven goals. U.S. women's national team defensive midfielder Lily Yohannes is getting more lethal in the tournament and scored in her second consecutive tournament match during OL's 6-0 blowout against Juventus.

Lily Yohannes makes it FOUR 💥The USWNT midfielder has now scored in back-to-back UWCL matches 🇺🇸🔥Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/9uLM309RM4.

The eight-time Champions League winners will go up against an English club with plenty of momentum following last week's results against Barcelona. The Gunners have more players available to shake things up on the pitch, and Alessia Russo remains a threat after her hat trick against Benfica and has four goals in the league phase.

Industry observers note that chelsea FC will host PSG and the Blues are riding high on stout defensive performances. They co-lead the tournament alongside OL Lyonnes with zero goals conceded through four league phase games.

The London side will need to be far better in attack if they want to claim being a top contender, though it's not for lack of trying. They're coming off a scoreless draw against BK Hacken, where they recorded a whopping 32 shots but only six attempts on target. U.S. women's national team winger Alyssa Thompson is still a factor with her swift technique and could help stretch PSG's backline, while Wieke Kaptein gets into dangerous spaces. Kaptein created both goals in Chelsea's 2-0 win against Roma, and the Dutch player has one goal and two assists in the tournament.

Recent findings suggest that PSG's fortunes seem to be turning for the worse after a promising start to the competition. They're in 10th place on the table now with five points and just one win in their last four games. The loss of Sakina Karchaoui with an ankle injury for the remainder of the league phase is a blow to the roster, though Naomie Feller, with two goals and two assists, is a threat for the Parisians.

It has been revealed that there are plenty of teams on the lower side of the table and running out of time. Alongside PSG with necessary urgency are Juventus, who were just beaten by OL Lyonnes, 6-0, and face a desperate 17th-place OH Leuven before closing out the league phase against PSG. It makes the penultimate meeting with OH Leuven almost a must win for Juventus, to lessen the stress on the final matchday.

A particularly intriguing matchup between ninth-place Benfica and 12th-place Roma could shake up the league table with a win by either side. If Roma's Kayleigh van Dooren and Alayah Pilgrim stay active on offense again, it could be a tough challenge for Benfica.
